titlePlain: Running as a Non-Root User, and Other
subtitle: Lesson 3 · Production-Grade Container Images

eyebrow: Least privilege, inside the container too

steps.label: No USER line = UID 0
steps.sub: root, unless the Dockerfile says otherwise

steps.label: Namespaces aren't a hypervisor
steps.sub: a container-escape bug is worse if root was already running

steps.label: Create a dedicated user
steps.sub: grant it only the directories it actually needs

code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN groupadd -r app && useradd -r -g app -d /app -s /sbin/nologin app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --chown=app:app . .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
USER app
CMD ["python", "main.py"]
caption: USER switches every following instruction, including CMD, to run unprivileged.

code:
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]
caption: runAsNonRoot makes the kubelet refuse to start the pod if the image would run as root.

steps.label: --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
steps.sub: root filesystem unwritable except explicit scratch space

steps.label: --cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE
steps.sub: re-add only the one capability actually needed

steps.label: --security-opt=no-new-privileges
steps.sub: blocks setuid-based privilege escalation at runtime
